mechanical.notes: 0 guard failures; boot clean; framing pass; negative control 13/13 (9 materials + 4 lighting). THE RIG WAS CONTRADICTING ITS OWN PRACTICALS: measured per-channel per-normal, an up-facing surface got BLUE light and a down-facing one got near-black ground bounce — the hemi sky and ground each described a DIFFERENT room than the one surface built (golden panels, wood floor). Both were defensible separately; nothing related them. Fixed exposure-preserving (luma 0.90->0.92, deliberate: moving the level would silently invalidate every albedo materials resolved against it). THE GUARD IS THE CONSTRUCTIVE ANSWER to the surface pass's guard-defends-a-false-premise finding: verifyRigAgreesWithItsPracticals compares the hemi sky against the CEILING PANEL EMISSIVE and the ground bounce against the FLOOR ALBEDO — MODEL against MODEL, not model against a typed constant. A GUARD THAT RELATES TWO PARTS OF THE MODEL CANNOT GO STALE: change the panel and the requirement on the rig changes with it, so it has no premise of its own to be wrong about; a guard written against a constant defends that constant forever (exactly how verifyLuminairesKeepTheirOwnHue ended up requiring the cold ceiling). Rule: prefer the relational form when the property is consistency between two things the model already contains; reserve constants for values from OUTSIDE the model (a published standard, a datasheet), noting the source beside them. Also fixed a LATENT camera-solver defect: when no radius within maxRadius framed the subject, the fallback returned r=12 IGNORING THE CAP (the cap exists so the camera does not pass through the aisle wall) — doesn't fire today (aisle 4.88/40, hero-rack 1.86/2.4) but the first pass to enlarge a subject would have stepped on it; now clamps to the cap and reports. Found by asking what the solver does when it FAILS, not watching it succeed.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The rig was quietly lighting the scene as two different rooms — blue sky on the golden panels, dark ground under the wood floor — because nothing related the light to the practicals it should agree with; fixed while holding the exposure so materials' work stays valid. The standout is the constructive close to the surface pass's deepest finding: a guard that RELATES two model parts (sky vs panel emissive, bounce vs floor albedo) cannot go stale, where a guard written against a typed constant defends that constant forever. The latent camera-fallback-ignores-the-cap defect, found by interrogating the failure path rather than the success path, is the same discipline. Framing holds, exposure held, negative control 13/13. Cleared to the interaction-ui pass, where the PDU pick() and the Axis transparency rule are finally due (the lounge glass and glass doors make them bearing).
